# c4factory Helm chart

Installs the whole C4 Factory: the operator, its CRDs and RBAC, the admission
policy (a Project is named after its namespace), the UI (it writes only Briefs
unless `ui.actions.enabled` is set), and Gitea,
seeded with the tagged templates, with its `base`, `go` and `image` CI runners. A device
installs [Agent Sandbox](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox)
itself, first. The Kind test environment installs with kustomize and `make`
instead (`make gitea seed deploy`); this chart is how a device installs it.

Most of it is generated by `make chart` (kubebuilder's helm plugin) from
`make build-installer`'s output; `make manifests` keeps `templates/crd/` and
`templates/rbac/manager-role.yaml` in step with `config/` on its own. `templates/ui/`, `templates/gitprovider/`, `templates/gitea/`,
`values.yaml` and `templates/NOTES.txt` are written by hand and survive a
regeneration; `Chart.yaml` is never overwritten.

## What the factory trusts

One install is one trust domain: install it on a device you own, for people
you would hand the Claude token to, and never on a shared or production
cluster. Anyone who can create a Project or a Brief in the cluster, the UI's
users included, can have the factory run code: in an agent's sandbox and in
a CI job. The sandbox holds no Claude token: the model proxy in the release
namespace adds it to the agent's requests, and the token never enters a
project namespace. The `base`, `go` and `image` runners run every project's checks and
image builds one after another in host mode, a NetworkPolicy keeping them to
DNS, Gitea and public HTTPS; the `image` runner's job container runs with
seccomp and AppArmor `Unconfined`, which rootless BuildKit needs ([#1076](https://github.com/JairJosafath/c4factory/issues/1076) gives
each job a pod of its own).
[docs/getting-started.md](../../docs/getting-started.md#what-the-factory-trusts)
says more.

## Install

[docs/getting-started.md](../../docs/getting-started.md) walks a device from
here to a first app the factory builds: the install below, the agents' Claude
token, a model, an Agent and a Crew, and a Gitea issue they turn into a merged
pull request.

1. **Agent Sandbox.** The operator runs its agents in Sandboxes and won't start
   without the `Sandbox` kind. The patch turns off its controller's leader
   election, which makes one replica exit on a busy host; run it alone on an
   install made without it ([the guide](../../docs/getting-started.md) says why).
   Install it before the chart: the chart lets the UI read pods in its
   namespace, `agent-sandbox-system`, which must exist:

   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/releases/download/v1.0.4/sandbox.yaml
   kubectl -n agent-sandbox-system patch deployment agent-sandbox-controller --type=json \
     -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/args/0","value":"--leader-elect=false"}]'
   ```

2. **The agents' token.** Make it once, in the release's namespace; the
   operator copies it into every project namespace and keeps the copies in
   step:

   ```bash
   kubectl create namespace c4-factory-system
   claude setup-token   # then:
   read -rs -p 'Claude token: ' T; echo; printf '%s' "$T" | kubectl -n c4-factory-system \
     create secret generic claude-credentials --from-file=CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=/dev/stdin; unset T
   ```

3. **The release.** On a fresh cluster Gitea's image may still be pulling when
   the seed starts, so give `helm install` time:

   ```bash
   helm install c4-factory oci://ghcr.io/jairjosafath/c4factory/charts/c4-factory --version VERSION \
     -n c4-factory-system --create-namespace --wait --timeout 10m \
     --set 'gitea.projects={webshop}'
   ```

The release requests about 2.1 CPU and 3.4 GiB of memory on top of
Kubernetes' own, most of it Gitea and the `go` and `image` runners; on a
two-CPU node, lower `runners.image.resources` and `runners.go.resources`, or
turn a runner off (`runners.go.enabled=false`; with `runners.image.enabled=false`
no release builds an image, its run waiting for a runner).

That is the whole factory. The chart made namespace `webshop`, labeled
`c4.factory.io/shared-secrets=true` and kept on uninstall like Gitea's; a
project namespace that already exists and the release didn't make (by hand, as
on v0.5.0) is left as it is, and the seed only adds the label
(`projectNamespaces.create=false`: you make every one). Upgrading from v0.5.0,
a `claude-credentials` you made in a project namespace by hand is unused now
(its agents reach Claude through the model proxy; delete it), and a `ghcr`
you made there stays that project's own; delete it to take the shared one.
The operator copies the release namespace's pull secrets into each labeled
namespace; the token is read by the model proxy there and never copied. Gitea runs in namespace `gitea`, at
`http://gitea.gitea.svc.cluster.local:3000` inside the cluster; the seed Job,
a hook after every install and upgrade, pushed the tagged templates to
organization `templates`, made organization `webshop`, stored its token in
Secret `webshop/gitea-credentials` and made Project `webshop` (only when the
namespace had none; it never changes one), and the chart made GitProvider
`webshop/gitea` from it. In `webshop` the chart also made the catalog, each
template the seed pushed pinned to its tag (`kubectl -n webshop get
c4catalog`), and Agents `planner`, `designer`, `reviewer` (Opus) and
`implementer` (Sonnet) on the release's `agent-go` image. The Agents read
Secret `webshop/claude-credentials`, key `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`: the
operator's copy of step 2's, or the project's own when you make one there,
which the operator never changes; the chart holds no token, and Project
`webshop`'s condition `SecretsShared` says which one it has. The chart
renders the GitProvider, the catalog and the Agents into ConfigMap
`gitea/c4factory-catalog`, and the seed applies them with server-side apply
(field manager `c4factory-chart`), so a `helm upgrade` changes them in place:
they keep their UIDs, a running Task keeps its Agent, a field you set that
the chart doesn't (an Agent's `env`) stays, and a field the chart sets is the
chart's. One the chart stops rendering stays until you delete it. Describe the
app in a Brief (the UI's box) and the planner writes the model, or apply your
own Systems and Containers to `webshop`; either way their repositories appear
in Gitea. The admin's password is in
Secret `gitea/gitea-admin`, which Gitea's pod made with a random password on
its first start (the chart renders no credential):

```bash
kubectl -n gitea get secret gitea-admin -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d; echo
kubectl -n gitea port-forward service/gitea 3000:3000   # http://localhost:3000
```

To rotate the admin's password, delete its Secret and restart Gitea's pod,
which makes a new one:

```bash
kubectl -n gitea delete secret gitea-admin
kubectl -n gitea rollout restart deployment/gitea
```

The shared runners register to the `templates` organization with the token
in Secret `gitea/gitea-runner`, which the seed fetches from Gitea on every
install and upgrade (Gitea hands out the same token until it is reset). They
serve the templates' checks only; each project's checks run on a pool of
single-job runner pods the operator keeps in the project's namespace. On an
upgrade from a chart whose runners registered to the instance, the running
runner pods keep that registration until restarted. To rotate the token,
reset it in Gitea (its runners page under the `templates` organization), then
delete the Secret, `helm upgrade` so the seed stores the new one, and restart
the runner Deployments:

```bash
kubectl -n gitea delete secret gitea-runner
helm upgrade ...   # the same command as the install
kubectl -n gitea rollout restart deployment/gitea-runner-base deployment/gitea-runner-go
```

With `gitea.admin.existingSecret` the admin is your Secret: change its
password there and restart Deployment `gitea`.

A new project later: add it to `gitea.projects` and `helm upgrade` with the
same values. `helm uninstall` keeps namespace `gitea` and Gitea's volume, so
the repositories survive a reinstall, and the project namespaces with their
models; delete a namespace to drop it.

An upgrade keeps your `c4.factory.io` objects valid: within `v1alpha1` a
release never removes, renames or retypes a field, never adds a required one
and never tightens a rule so that an object applied before is refused after;
a change that must break waits for a `v1beta1` that converts them. See
[Compatibility](../../docs/design.md#compatibility).

### Private images

The chart and the images on GHCR are private until the owner makes them
public. A device pulls them with a GitHub token that has `read:packages`
(`gh auth refresh -s read:packages`, then `gh auth token`). Helm pulls the
chart, so log it in first, whichever way the images come:

```bash
gh auth token | helm registry login ghcr.io -u "$(gh api user -q .login)" --password-stdin
```

The images come in one of two ways:

- **A pull secret.** Make a `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` Secret in the
  release's namespace and in Gitea's, and name it in `global.imagePullSecrets`
  (the UI, Gitea, the seed and the runners) and `manager.imagePullSecrets`
  (the operator):

  ```bash
  for ns in c4-factory-system gitea; do
    kubectl create namespace $ns --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
    kubectl -n $ns create secret docker-registry ghcr --docker-server=ghcr.io \
      --docker-username=USER --docker-password="$(gh auth token)"
  done
  helm install ... --set gitea.createNamespace=false \
    --set 'global.imagePullSecrets[0].name=ghcr' \
    --set 'manager.imagePullSecrets[0].name=ghcr'
  ```

  The Secret has to exist before Gitea's pods, so you make namespace `gitea`
  and the chart doesn't (`gitea.createNamespace=false`). The agent images
  (`agent-base`, `agent-go`) run in Sandboxes the operator makes in each
  project namespace: it copies each of `global.imagePullSecrets` there from
  the release's namespace and names it in their pods, so a project namespace
  needs no Secret or ServiceAccount patch of its own.

- **Kind: load them.** `docker login ghcr.io`, `docker pull` each image at the
  release's version and `kind load docker-image` it into the cluster; no pull
  secret.

A `vX.Y.Z` tag publishes the chart and its images: the *Release* workflow
(`.github/workflows/release.yml`) pushes the chart to
`oci://ghcr.io/jairjosafath/c4factory/charts`, attaches it to the GitHub release
and pushes `ghcr.io/jairjosafath/c4factory/<name>:X.Y.Z` for `operator`, `ui`, `seed`,
the toolchains `base` and `go`, `agent-base`, `agent-go`, `gitea-runner-base`
and `gitea-runner-go` (all `linux/amd64`). A released chart runs its own
version's operator and UI images. From a checkout, `helm install ... dist/chart`
with `--set manager.image.tag=...` and `--set ui.image.tag=...` installs images
you built and pushed yourself.

A release can be checked by hand: once *Release* has published it, the
*Verify Release* workflow (`.github/workflows/verify-release.yml`),
dispatched from the Actions page, installs that version's chart from
GHCR on Kind, as above, scaffolds the webshop sample's `orders-api`, then
follows [getting-started](../../docs/getting-started.md) up to the first app's
scaffold and an `Idle` Crew (no Agent runs). The
result is on the repository's Actions page (Verify Release, with the evidence
as the run's artifact); a failing release gets an issue titled
`Release vX.Y.Z fails its check`.

## Values

| Value | What it sets |
| --- | --- |
| `manager.image`, `ui.image` | repository, tag (default `Chart.appVersion`), pullPolicy |
| `manager.args` | the operator's flags (`go run ./cmd --help`); the defaults are the Kind environment's |
| `sessionBinaryURL` | where scaffolded devcontainers download `c4session`, the Session client (`--session-binary-url`, `${arch}` becomes `amd64` or `arm64`); default the UI, whose image carries the client under `/downloads/`: `http://localhost:<ui.service.port>/...` for the port-forward, `https://<ui.allowedHosts[0]>/...` behind an Ingress, so a private repository's release needs no GitHub login. The devcontainer's build must reach that address (a port-forward's localhost is the laptop's, not a container's), so set one it reaches when it doesn't. With `ui.enabled` false, the binaries attached to this chart's GitHub release. Both serve a `SHA256SUMS` next to the binaries, which the feature checks the download against; a URL of your own needs one too. Empty sets none |
| `ui.enabled` | install the UI (default true); `ui.service` and `ui.resources` |
| `ui.allowedHosts` | host names the UI answers besides localhost, for an Ingress in front of it; any other Host is refused |
| `ui.actions.enabled` | off by default; on, the UI also sets Brief and Crew settings, re-runs a failed release, retries a scaffold, makes a Task from a goal and bumps a Standard's ref (design.md, *UI actions*). Over port-forward its ServiceAccount makes them; with `ui.allowedHosts` the chart needs `ui.auth.oidc` |
| `ui.auth.oidc` | sign-in for the actions: `issuerURL`, `clientID` and `existingSecret` (a Secret you make, key `client-secret` or `existingSecretKey`) required; `redirectURL`, `scopes`, `usernameClaim` (`email`), `usernamePrefix` (`oidc:`), `groupsClaim` (`groups`), `groupsPrefix` (`oidc:`), `actionGroups`. A person signs in from the UI's top bar (**Sign in**, or `/ui/login`) and every write is made as them; the UI's ServiceAccount gets `impersonate` on users and groups ([getting started](../../docs/getting-started.md#ui-actions-behind-an-ingress)) |
| `ui.components` | the UI health view's components; an empty namespace is the release's |
| `gitea.enabled` | install Gitea, the seed and the runners (default true); off, `gitProviders` point at a Gitea of your own |
| `gitea.namespace`, `gitea.createNamespace` | Gitea's namespace (default `gitea`) and whether the chart makes it |
| `gitea.image`, `gitea.resources`, `gitea.persistence`, `gitea.config` | Gitea's image, its share of the node, its volume and extra `GITEA__section__KEY` settings |
| `gitea.admin` | the admin's name and email; `existingSecret` for one of your own, else the password is generated |
| `gitea.projects` | project names: a namespace each (see `projectNamespaces.create`), labeled `c4.factory.io/shared-secrets=true` by the chart or the seed, with an organization, Secret `gitea-credentials`, GitProvider `gitea` and, when there is none, Project `<name>` |
| `projectNamespaces.create` | make each of `gitea.projects`' namespaces, kept on uninstall, unless it exists and isn't the release's (default on); off, you make them and the seed labels them |
| `gitea.seed.image`, `gitea.seed.waitSeconds` | the seed Job's image (default tag `Chart.appVersion`) and how long it waits for Gitea |
| `catalog.enabled`, `catalog.entries` | for each of `gitea.projects`, the catalog entries of the templates the seed pushes (Frameworks, Standards, Compute, Deployments, Connectors), each pinned to its tag in `templates/versions.txt` (default on) |
| `agents.enabled`, `agents.image`, `agents.credentialsSecret` | for each of `gitea.projects`, Agents `planner`, `designer`, `implementer` and `reviewer` on the agent image (default `agent-go`, tag `Chart.appVersion`), reading the Secret you make once in the release's namespace (default `claude-credentials`), which the model proxy reads there; never copied into a project namespace (default on) |
| `agents.modelProxy` | the model proxy, with `agents.enabled`: the operator image running `/model-proxy` in the release namespace as Service `c4-model-proxy` on 8080, the one place the token is used, mounted from `agents.credentialsSecret` as an optional volume (the proxy is ready before the Secret exists and answers 503 until it does) and reached only by agent sandboxes (a NetworkPolicy); `replicas` (default 2, with a PodDisruptionBudget above 1), `upstream` (default `https://api.anthropic.com`), `drainSeconds` (default 5) and `resources` ([the plan](../../docs/plans/done/model-proxy.md)) |
| `agents.standIn` | for each of `gitea.projects`, Agent `stand-in` on the same image: no model and no Secret, it plans from the catalog and makes a scripted change, to show the loop without a token (default on; off with `agents.enabled=false` too) |
| `agents.<role>` | each Agent's `description`, `model` (Opus, Sonnet for the implementer; a Fable model fails the install), `maxRounds`, `timeoutMinutes` and `resources` |
| `runners.base`, `runners.go`, `runners.image` | the CI runners: `enabled`, `image`, `replicas` (default 1), `resources`, `workSize`, `tmpSize`; `go.goCache` is the node directory of its Go build cache; `image.buildkit` runs its job container as rootless BuildKit needs, with its work and tmp directories on disk |
| `global.imagePullSecrets` | pull secrets for the UI, Gitea, the seed and the runners, which the operator also copies into each project namespace for the agents' pods; the operator's are `manager.imagePullSecrets` |
| `gitProviders` | more GitProviders to create, each reading a Secret you make (`existingSecret`), below |
| `crd.enabled`, `crd.keep` | install the CRDs with the chart; keep them on uninstall (default) |
| `metrics`, `prometheus`, `networkPolicy` | the generated metrics endpoint, ServiceMonitor and NetworkPolicy |

### Git providers

Each Project namespace needs a GitProvider: where its Containers' repositories
are created. `gitea.projects` makes them for the release's Gitea; for a Gitea
of your own (`gitea.enabled=false`), the chart can create them:

```yaml
gitProviders:
  - namespace: webshop          # must exist
    name: gitea
    provider: gitea
    url: http://gitea.gitea.svc.cluster.local:3000
    owner: webshop              # the organization holding the repositories
    existingSecret: git-credentials
```

The chart renders no Secret: the token is yours, so you make the Secret, with
keys `username` and `token`, before the install:

```bash
kubectl -n webshop create secret generic git-credentials \
  --from-literal=username=c4factory --from-literal=token="$GIT_TOKEN"
```

`gitProviders[].token` and `username` are gone (they put the token in your
values file and in every revision of Helm's release record); a values file
that still sets them fails to render and says what to do.

The CRDs are part of the release, so the GitProviders are not release objects:
the chart renders them into ConfigMap `c4factory-gitproviders`, and Job
`c4-factory-gitproviders`, a `post-install` and `post-upgrade` hook on the seed
image (`gitea.seed.image`), applies them in place with server-side apply, under
a Role in each `gitProviders[].namespace` that grants only GitProviders. An
upgrade changes them in place, keeping their UIDs and any field the chart
doesn't set, so a Git step in flight never misses its GitProvider; the first
upgrade from an older chart takes over the hooks it made. `helm uninstall`
leaves them in place, as it does one the chart stops rendering. The
GitProviders `gitea.projects` makes are applied the same way, by the seed.
